skill.name: design-lint
skill.description: A deterministic design linter for standalone HTML and rendered pages. It checks CSS token hygiene, accessibility signals, layout issues, and common visual anti-patterns without using an LLM.
skill.summary: Run deterministic checks for design tokens, accessibility, and CSS consistency.
skill.author: cubha

security_audit.summary: All 134 static matches are false positives caused by Markdown, JavaScript template literals, CSS regular expressions, and local file-reading utilities. The reviewed implementation contains no process-spawning API, network client, credential handling, data exfiltration, obfuscation payload, or prompt-injection content.

remediation.issue: The linter accepts paths for local HTML, token, and observation files.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should lint only trusted local inputs, or add optional path allowlisting for automated environments.

remediation.issue: Synchronous reads can delay a process when inputs are large.
remediation.suggestion: Use asynchronous file APIs or enforce input-size limits if the tool will run on untrusted or very large files.

content.user_title: Check designs with deterministic CSS rules
content.value_statement: Design reviews can vary between reviewers and slow down delivery. This skill applies repeatable checks to HTML and CSS so teams can catch token, layout, and accessibility issues before release.
actual_capabilities: Scans inline CSS and style attributes in standalone HTML files.
Checks hard-coded colors and spacing against a supplied DESIGN-TOKENS.md file.
Reports readability, focus-outline, motion, spacing, typography, and layout warnings.
Produces a structured JSON report with error and warning counts.
Uses an optional gate mode that exits with status 1 for error-severity findings.
Accepts browser-collected observations for contrast, target size, and overflow checks.
limitations: Regex analysis is designed for standalone HTML with inline styles, not every external stylesheet or framework build.
Token hygiene checks require a suitable DESIGN-TOKENS.md file.
Browser-derived checks require a fixed viewport and collected observation data.
Warnings identify heuristic anti-patterns and still require design judgment.

use_cases.title: Review a design prototype
use_cases.description: Check a standalone prototype before sharing it with stakeholders. The report identifies token drift and common CSS consistency issues.

use_cases.title: Add a CI design gate
use_cases.description: Run the linter after generating HTML artifacts. Use gate mode to stop the pipeline only for error-severity findings.

use_cases.title: Audit a deployed page
use_cases.description: Collect computed-style observations from a fixed browser viewport and inspect contrast, target size, and overflow signals.

prompt_templates.title: Lint one prototype
prompt_templates.prompt: Run design-lint on docs/design/prototype/home.html and summarize the errors and warnings.

prompt_templates.title: Check design tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Run design-lint on docs/design/prototype/*.html using docs/design/DESIGN-TOKENS.md. List token hygiene violations first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: validate a tokenized prototype set.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a CI gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Run design-lint with --gate on the generated HTML files. Report the JSON verdict and the findings that block the pipeline.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: use the result in continuous integration.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a rendered page
prompt_templates.prompt: At a fixed 1280 by 800 viewport, collect the required browser observations for this rendered page. Run design-lint with the observations and explain any contrast, target-size, or overflow findings.

output_examples.input: Lint a prototype with a token file.
output: Count of error and warning findings
Named detector results with file and evidence

output_examples.input: Run gate mode after a generated HTML build.
output: A nonzero exit status when error findings exist
A JSON summary for the CI log
Warnings that remain visible without blocking the build

output_examples.input: Analyze a rendered page with browser observations.
output: A note when observation-dependent checks were skipped

best_practices: Provide the project token file when token hygiene matters.
Use a fixed viewport before collecting browser observations.
Treat warnings as review prompts and verify them in the rendered interface.
anti_patterns: Do not use this tool as a substitute for human visual design review.
Do not enable gate mode until token files and thresholds match the project standards.
Do not treat skipped browser-observation checks as evidence that a page is accessible.

faq.question: Does this skill use an LLM to judge a design?
faq.answer: No. Its detectors are deterministic functions that return the same result for the same input.

faq.question: What files can it inspect?
faq.answer: It is designed for standalone HTML files with inline style blocks or style attributes.

faq.question: Why should I provide DESIGN-TOKENS.md?
faq.answer: The file supplies the approved color and spacing values for token hygiene checks.

faq.question: What does gate mode do?
faq.answer: With --gate, error-severity findings cause the command to exit with status 1. Warnings do not block the command.

faq.question: Can it inspect a live URL?
faq.answer: Yes, when a browser workflow renders the page and provides normalized HTML plus computed-style observations.

faq.question: Does a warning mean the design is wrong?
faq.answer: No. Warnings flag heuristic patterns that may be intentional and should be reviewed by a designer.
